title: The Autopsy of Windrow House
premise: When the coffin of town founder Edmund Windrow is exhumed for a cemetery relocation and found empty, night-shift taxi dispatcher Marguerite Ashgrove recognizes the signature of a cover-up — the same one behind three 'accidental' deaths they quietly solved years ago. Following dispatch logs, fare records, and the testimony of a witness officially declared dead, Marguerite uncovers that Windrow faked his own death in 1974 to escape prosecution, and that the town's founding families have been killing to keep it buried. In the end, Marguerite corners the last living conspirator at Windrow House itself, chooses justice over vengeance by forcing a confession on tape rather than a second murder, and finds their found family — the drivers, the coroner's clerk, and the 'dead' witness herself — waiting when dawn comes.
about_author: Juniper Quintana spent six years answering phones at a small-town cab company before turning the dispatcher's ear for other people's emergencies into fiction. They live in a converted funeral parlor with two cats named after cold cases.

chapters.title: The Fare Nobody Called For
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A slow night shift; a cab is dispatched to Windrow House for a passenger who never appears, and the driver returns shaken by lights moving inside the sealed house. Marguerite files it away with the same instinct that once solved three 'accidents.' Beat: quiet competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Exhumation
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The cemetery relocation forces Edmund Windrow's famous grave open before a crowd; the coffin holds only river stones and a 1974 newspaper. The mayor calls it vandalism. Marguerite notices the coffin was sealed from inside. Beat: the past cracking open.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Flashback-woven chapter, Marguerite's POV. We learn how Marguerite solved three deaths the police closed as accidents — a drowned fisherman, a garage fire, a fall on ice — all connected to Windrow family land deeds. Beat: establishing the price of knowing too much.

chapters.title: The Coroner's Clerk
chapters.summary: POV: Dev Okonkwo, the coroner's clerk who once helped Marguerite quietly. He confirms the exhumed remains were swapped decades ago with institutional complicity. Someone has already searched his office. Beat: alliance renewed, fear shared.

chapters.title: Dispatch Logs, 1974
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. In the taxi company's basement archive, Marguerite finds a 1974 logbook: a cab ran the same impossible route the night Windrow 'died' — from the river to the train station, paid in cash. Beat: the thrill of the hunt sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: The Widow Who Isn't
chapters.summary: POV: Celeste Windrow, the founder's elderly daughter-in-law, who knows more than she says and warns Marguerite off with genuine terror. She slips a key into Marguerite's coat pocket. Beat: sympathy entangled with suspicion.

chapters.title: House of River Stones
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Using the key, Marguerite enters Windrow House at night and finds a room preserved like a shrine — and evidence someone has been living there recently. Footsteps above. Escape through the servant stairs. Beat: violation and adrenaline.

chapters.title: A Witness Declared Dead
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Records reveal Lena Marsh, the state's star witness against Windrow in 1974, died in a car crash before testifying — but her death certificate bears the same forged signature as the three 'accidents.' Beat: the pattern confirmed.

chapters.title: The Found Family Table
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At the all-night diner, Marguerite lays out the case to the cab drivers who've become their true family. Half urge them to stop; one, Rosa, admits her father drove that 1974 fare and never spoke of it again. Beat: loyalty tested.

chapters.title: What Rosa's Father Knew
chapters.summary: Rosa's POV. Rosa opens her late father's locked toolbox and finds a photograph: Windrow alive at a bus depot in 1975, and a note — 'He pays us to forget.' Beat: inherited silence, generational complicity.

chapters.title: Pressure
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite's tires are slashed, then an anonymous offer arrives: a generous settlement to leave town. The message names the diner, the drivers, Dev. Beat: the cost of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: Celeste Breaks
chapters.summary: Celeste's POV. Cornered by Marguerite's questions, Celeste confesses the family secret: Edmund didn't die; he fled embezzlement charges, and each generation has paid to keep him gone — including arranging Lena Marsh's death. Beat: grief disguised as duty.

chapters.title: Lena Marsh, Alive
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Cross-referencing pension payments and pharmacy records, Marguerite traces a woman living under another name two towns over — the witness everyone swears is dead. Beat: hope arriving like a held breath.

chapters.title: The Woman at the End of the Route
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena, old and watchful, tells Marguerite what really happened in 1974: she saw Windrow board that cab alive, and she's survived fifty years by being no one. She refuses to testify. Beat: the price of survival embodied.

chapters.title: Murder, Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Dev discovers the current conspiracy isn't protecting Windrow anymore — he truly is dead now, killed weeks ago inside Windrow House, and the empty-coffin scandal threatens the heirs' trust fund. Someone plans to make Marguerite the fourth accident. Beat: stakes turn lethal.

chapters.title: Rosa Drives Into It
chapters.summary: Rosa's POV. Rosa picks up a fare to Windrow House and realizes too late she's bait. Marguerite, tracking the cab from dispatch, reroutes every unit in the fleet to shadow her. Beat: the found family becoming a rescue network.

chapters.title: The Heir Apparent
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Evidence points to Julian Windrow, Edmund's great-grandson, who learned the truth while settling the estate and killed his ancestor to keep the money flowing. But the police chief — a founding-family name — won't hear it. Beat: justice outside the law becomes necessity.

chapters.title: Tape
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite devises a plan: lure Julian into confessing using the one thing he can't resist — the threat that Lena Marsh is ready to talk. Dev wires the diner booth. Beat: cold clarity before the storm.

chapters.title: Windrow House, Last Night
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian takes the bait but smells the trap, abducts Marguerite at knifepoint, and forces them to Windrow House to destroy the recording and stage their death among the river stones. Beat: terror, and Marguerite talking to survive.

chapters.title: The Confession
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. In the shrine room, Marguerite keeps Julian talking — about his grandfather's payments, about Edmund's murder — while the drivers, tipped by dispatch radio, surround the house with headlights and phones recording. Dev arrives with state police. Beat: the climax; voice as weapon.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. With Julian arrested, Lena walks into the courthouse she avoided for fifty years and gives her statement, choosing to be someone again. Celeste testifies to the family's payments. Beat: justice finally wearing a lawful face.

chapters.title: Morning Shift
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Weeks later, the diner table is full, Rosa's father's name is cleared publicly, and Marguerite takes one last dispatch call to Windrow House — now a museum — and lets it go unanswered. Beat: peace earned, family chosen, the night shift finally quiet.
